quest.title: World-Order Narration
quest.description: As Dainsleif guessed, the "false memories" are a trap laid by the Abyss Order. The Ley Lines are disturbed again. Something is probably underway once more...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1125, Primogem x60, Mora x49200, Guide to Equity x2, Guide to Justice x2, Guide to Order x2, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x9

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there! It looks like they're sleeping...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: ...In the end, he whispered softly,

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: "Sleep well, Father. Sleep well, my beloved people."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: "When you awake, that which differentiates us shall be no more."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look at those Hilichurls over there...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They seem strangely... calm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weren't they acting super agitated just a little while ago? Why are they so calm all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait... I hear something...)

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: ...In the new world, they bade farewell to the shrouded sun.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: At last, they no longer needed to dwell on their suffering, or try to differentiate between various thoughts of blasphemy.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: Such was the price they paid, and thus their souls became cleansed and pure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the same thing is happening over here too. The Hilichurls are calm...

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: ...You see? We're both still here.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: We've reclaimed an endless amount of time to love.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Voice
dialogues.text: Release your tears. You no longer need to hold back your sorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grandpa Amadhiah, is everyone alright? The Abyss Order seems to be up to something nearby...

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: The Abyss Order? This is the first I'm hearing of it...

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Thank you for your concern, but as far as I'm aware, it's been business as usual here in the village.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's good to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Also... You didn't happen to come across any clues about the missing villager while we were gone, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Huh? Someone's gone missing, you say? Who would that be?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh...?

choices.text: You don't remember?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know... The young guy from Vimara Village... The one you've been looking for all this time. You posted a commission with the Sumeru Adventurers' Guild...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's kind of the whole reason we're here, actually... Your missing person's commission.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Ah, I do apologize, you two... I hope I'm not worrying you too much. I'm sure it's just my age making me forgetful again...

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: At least right now, I can't seem to recall whatever it is you're referring to... Perhaps you should try asking someone else?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, how is that... *sigh* Alright. Thanks for your help, Grandpa Amadhiah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something's definitely not right. We just talked to Grandpa Amadhiah about the missing villager. There's no way he could've forgotten all about him just like that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Could everyone's memories of the missing villager have been erased again?

choices.text: It's too early to say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right. We should narrow down the possibilities first... Let's go ask someone else, then!

choices.text: We should check in with the others first.
Things just got even more complicated.

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: Someone's gone missing? Who?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Just as expected...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, that guy you said a bunch of nice things about earlier? The one you always used to chat with...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's around twenty years old... You said he was a kind, warm-hearted sort of person...

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: Oh! I know who you're talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? You remember?

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: There aren't many young people who've earned that kind of praise from me. If you're certain that's what I said...

dialogues.speaker: Bahram
dialogues.text: Then, there's only person who fits the bill — no doubt about it... But, why'd you say he's gone missing?

choices.text: Have you seen him recently?

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: Yeah! I just saw him leave the village. There was someone else with him too. They couldn't have gone far.

choices.text: Do you know where he went?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! That's exactly what Atossa described!

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, every time we talked, it always seemed to be around dusk, just like right now.

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Time always passed by really slowly. Even when it felt like we'd been talking for hours, the sun would still be at the same position in the sky...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, that has to be it! This is definitely Atossa's memory!

choices.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That's where they'll be!

choices.text: To the tree.

talks.objective: Go to the place Atossa once indicated

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're... Caribert Alberich.

dialogues.speaker: Caribert
dialogues.text: Oh... You know me? That's quite the surprise. I don't believe I've met you before...

dialogues.speaker: Caribert
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. It was the memory, wasn't it? Your sibling's memory. You saw... the me from back then.

dialogues.speaker: Caribert
dialogues.text: This is Atossa's memory. I came here to say goodbye to her...

dialogues.speaker: Caribert
dialogues.text: But, I suppose I'll just leave her a message instead. Come, let's find somewhere else to talk...

dialogues.speaker: Caribert
dialogues.text: *panting*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Caribert
dialogues.text: I suppose you could call it the realm of my consciousness. I'm someone who no longer exists in the real world, after all... as you well know.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You look quite exhausted.

dialogues.speaker: Caribert
dialogues.text: Ah, it's nothing. I still have enough strength to play the part of a good host. I've always hoped that I'd get the chance to talk to you like this, and now, the time has finally arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is a rare opportunity for me as well. I should try to learn as much information from Caribert as I can.)

choices.text: What exactly happened to you?

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Extreme sorrow and pain... Hope and regret coursing through your veins... and a degree of Abyssal power that defies comprehension...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Father told me that once I possessed all those elements, I would become the Loom of Fate.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: But, despite his intentions for me, I never truly became the Loom of Fate. I was merely used as a means for its "construction"...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: In truth, I died the moment I set everything in motion.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: The "person" you see before you now is nothing but a remnant of consciousness leftover within the Loom of Fate.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Caribert is dead... That's why he no longer exists outside of people's memories.)

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: As for your question... The Loom of Fate is a device capable of weaving Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Weaving... Ley Lines?

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: In its primitive form, it can only be used to create and implant memories. But, as more of it is completed, its power becomes stronger and stronger... Until finally, it has the power to weave real Ley Lines of its own.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Once fully completed, the moment it gains the power to weave Ley Lines, it loses the lower-level ability to influence memories...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: ...But it also becomes a tool that can change the entire world.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So that was the source of your ability to implant memories?

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Yes. I have the ability to control the Loom in its semi-completed form. I suppose you could think of it as a form of compensation...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: ...After all, its existence cost me my life.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So the memories that suddenly appeared in Dain's mind were implanted by Caribert through the half-finished Loom of Fate...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That makes sense... But, I'm still lost as to why he went so far as to "introduce" himself to all the residents of Vimara Village...)

choices.text: But why did you implant memories of yourself...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Ah, that... I was wrong to implant those memories. I'm sorry I caused so much trouble, not only for everyone in the village, but for you as well.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: I just... wanted them to feel like I once existed in this world...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: As if... I had a chance at life.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So that's why... I would have never guessed.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But... is there any kind of meaning to this?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Does only existing in people's memories really count as living?)

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: ...Heh, I know what you must be thinking...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Why would I do something so meaningless...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: But I just... I just couldn't accept it.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: I had to know what it would be like if I had my own life — what kind of person I would be, what other people would think of me...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Chief Amadhiah, Bahram, Granny Jehiet... Atossa...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: What would it be like if I could live alongside them — no cataclysm, no curse, just a quiet life in a peaceful village.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: I was curious, so I selfishly... tried to have my own life.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Even if... Even if that meant piecing together the version of myself that could have been... one memory at a time.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: I know it sounds stupid, hehe...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: After all... my life ended a long time ago.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Any chance at living was stripped away from me when I was eight years old, my consciousness left to mature in an illusory world of nothingness.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Even the form you see before you is nothing but an invention based on my father's appearance — an imagined version of what I would look like if I had had the chance to grow up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...In the end, this all stems from the tragedy that occurred in Khaenri'ah back then...)

choices.text: You know...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: I know... But, there's nothing I can do to make them find me.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: If I could exist in the real world, I would return without a second thought and surprise them with the suddenness of it all. But, well... That's not possible for me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: As I understand it...

choices.text: Even though you only appeared in their memories...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They all believe you once lived among them.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: I know.

choices.text: Well, now that I've found you, let's continue this conversation some other time.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Captain Dainsleif, Twilight Sword, you mean? Ah, no need to meet up with him. Things should already be settled on his end.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Settled?

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Exactly. As someone who could only exist in people's memories, the fact that I'm able to talk to you in my consciousness like this can only mean one thing...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: The Loom of Fate has already been completed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Loom of Fate is already complete? That means the eye of the first Field Tiller must have fallen into the hands of the Abyss... Could something have happened to Dain?)

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: No need to worry about Captain Dainsleif. He's absolutely fine. The only reason he lost the eye was because I happened to guess exactly what he was planning.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Captain Dainsleif has had the eye inside his body this whole time, hasn't he?

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: #His plan was to lure the Abyss Order to a false location, capitalizing on their pursuit of the eye in order to have the chance to confront the {M#princess}{F#prince}...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: He would then hand the eye to you, and tell you to take it away from that location.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: That way, Captain Dainsleif could accomplish his own goal and ensure the safety of the eye all at once — a very thorough plan.

choices.text: But...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: That's right. Because, in his mind... he had given it to you already.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, does that mean he gave Dain a... false memory!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You made him think that! When?

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Before you two entered that false location...

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, wait...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hm?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: ...We've no time to lose. Let's head inside.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So when Dain froze up back then, it was because a false memory was being implanted in his mind... No wonder...)

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: That was when I implanted the memory of him handing you the eye.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Given the tense situation at that time, Captain Dainsleif failed to notice anything out of the ordinary and took that memory to be real.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: #...I'm sorry, {NICKNAME}, but I needed the Loom of Fate to be completed, and to do that, we had to retrieve the eye.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So, Dain had the eye this whole time... until the Abyss Order took it away. I'm not sure there's anything we could have done.)

choices.text: Now that the Loom of Fate is complete...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: #I promise I'm not trying to conceal anything from you... But, I truly have no idea what the {M#princess}{F#prince} is planning.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: Teyvat's Ley Line system is deeply entrenched in the planet. Creating new Ley Lines can neither "replace" nor "extend" the ones that already exist...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: In the face of everything they could be planning, I fear I'm too insignificant to even get a glimpse of the bigger picture.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: In any case, I had my own use for the Loom of Fate, and my goal, at least, has been achieved.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your goal?

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: You remember my father, don't you? Chlothar Alberich. I believe you saw him in your sibling's memory.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: After he used the power of the Abyss to restore consciousness to my Hilichurl form, I suffered from an indescribable level of mental anguish.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: To comfort me, my father told me a story... That this was a fairytale world, where I had to take on the form of a little monster...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: That story managed to dispel my fears... even if just for a moment.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: My goal was simple — to use the Loom of Fate in its near-completed form, when its ability to create memories was at its strongest...

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: To implant a specific memory into the minds of the Hilichurls.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: In that memory, I would tell them a story... just like my father did for me. It was a story of fairy tales and love... But, more than anything, it was the story of us.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So the thing that caused the Hilichurls to calm down back then was Caribert's story...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So that was his goal... That was the only thing he wanted.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (He had a device as powerful as the Loom of Fate at his disposal, and all he wanted to do with it was to offer the Hilichurls a moment of comfort and peace...)

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: I can't change the world, not when I lost the very right to exist within it. Implanting those memories... that was the most worthwhile thing I could offer.

choices.text: Perhaps.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: All that's left of my existence is a wisp of residual consciousness tied to the Loom of Fate. In truth, that trace of my consciousness should have dissipated long ago... My goal was the one thing that allowed me to hold on all this time.

response.speaker: Caribert
response.text: But now, the bedtime story... is finished, and it's finally time to rest.

choices.text: I think... It was very meaningful indeed.
What are you planning on doing with it?
Dain never handed me the eye.
Dain might still need my help...
Your existence was a great comfort to them.
Everyone is looking for you.
Into the people of Vimara Village?
What exactly is the Loom of Fate?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: Well... How about a conversation?

dialogues.speaker: Sibling
dialogues.text: The chance to just stop and talk like this is certainly not easy to come by... Wouldn't you agree?

choices.text: Yeah.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: That battle earlier was tough...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: The one against Dain, I mean.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: I didn't expect that after everything, he would still hesitate to raise his sword against me...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Were it not for that... Perhaps I'd still be no match for the Twilight Sword. Even after five hundred years.

choices.text: What exactly are you planning?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: The Loom of Fate, huh... I still haven't found a way to utilize it to its full potential, but there's still time...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: ...Before the Heavenly Principles "awaken."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Heavenly Principles are still asleep?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Yes, for five hundred years now, ever since the cataclysm in Khaenri'ah. There's been no sign of activity...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Not long ago, you witnessed the Hydro Archon destroy her divine throne, yes?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Such a flagrant disregard for the "rules," and still Celestia took no action... I suppose that's proof enough of the Heavenly Principles' situation.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: However, the Heavenly Principles will awaken... We just don't know when that will be, or what might trigger it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You really hate the Heavenly Principles, don't you?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: You could say that.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Just look at Caribert. He was so pure and single-minded... The space we now find ourselves is a perfect representation of who he was — quiet and peaceful.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Even as a Hilichurl, seeing the terrible sight within the mirror wasn't enough to taint his spirit.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: He brought comfort to the people of this world... even though he was denied the very right to be a part of it...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: So, ask yourself this... Who was it that deprived him of that right to exist?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Of course, that's only one example. My feelings about the Heavenly Principles are too complicated to explain in just a few words...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: #...{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}?

response.speaker: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}
response.text: You're the only one in this world who calls me that.

response.speaker: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}
response.text: There's so much I wanted to ask you, but for some reason, I'm not interested in asking those questions right now.

response.speaker: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}
response.text: There's just one thing I have to ask, one thing I could never understand...

response.speaker: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}
response.text: Why... Why can't we continue our journey together?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: At the end of my journey, I arrived at a place known as "The Sea of Flowers at the End."

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Do you remember? A long time ago, when we traveled between worlds together...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: You told me... You wanted to find a place in the universe where that one flower was in full bloom.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: To have a place like that suddenly appear before me...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Well, would you think of that as a coincidence?

response.speaker: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}
response.text: You mean...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: #I miss you too, {M#Aether}{F#Lumine}.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: But as this war continues to rage, and as I continue to seek that final answer...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: #I don't even know how to face myself sometimes... let alone my own {M#brother}{F#sister}.

response.speaker: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}
response.text: What's going on?

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: This space has lost its tether... I doubt it'll be able to exist much longer.

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: In fact, aside from our inability to physically interact with each other, there's something else you should know about this space. With Caribert gone, we won't be able to remember anything that happened here...

response.speaker: Sibling
response.text: Everything in this space will be wiped from existence... including all memory of our reunion.

response.speaker: #{M#Aether}{F#Lumine}
response.text: You're only telling me this now...

choices.text: What are you going to do with the Loom of Fate?
I almost can't believe it's real.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*... So sleepy. Paimon's head still feels all fuzzy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon woke up a little earlier than you, so Paimon will fill you in. The villagers said they saw us sleeping near the village yesterday. They couldn't wake us up no matter how hard they tried, so they decided to just bring us back here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and Dain came by just now. It looked like he was injured...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He didn't say anything, though. Just made sure that you were alright and left... Kinda seemed like he had a lot on his mind... But, that's Dain for you...

choices.text: He never changes, does he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, let's think for a second. We were in that memory, and we saw that guy you called Caribert...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He was the missing villager we'd been trying to find, right? And after that... Paimon doesn't remember what happened...

choices.text: Caribert and I talked for a while...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, really? What a score!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I guess our commission is complete, then. The missing villager, the person who only existed in people's memories, was Caribert all along...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But, now that he's gone, I'm not sure how to explain things to the villagers...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... What happened after that?

choices.text: After that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Maybe I'm just tired? I feel like something else happened, but why can't I remember...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I'm not sure why... But, it almost feels like I lost something...)

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: Ah, there you are! Haha, sleep well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bahram? You sure seem happy. Did something good happen?

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: Something good? Hm... wasn't anything good or bad, I'd say.

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: It's just that, well... The village organized another search party yesterday. It didn't feel right to leave all the searching to the adventurers.

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: So there we were, searching away, when suddenly this one guy said it all came back to him...

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: According to him, one day around dusk, he was passing by this one tree outside the village, and he saw our missing villager.

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: There he was, sleeping under that tree all by himself. His parents came a little later to wake him up, and they all left together. They looked like quite a happy family, apparently.

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: And, after that, well... We all started to feel like that really is what happened... Kinda strange that we forgot all about it for so long...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So, that's how Caribert said his goodbyes... That was the last memory he gave them.)

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: Oh, and we also remembered his name — Caribert. Now, that's not a name you hear everyday. Would've been helpful if we remembered it sooner.

choices.text: That is a unique name.

response.speaker: Bahram
response.text: Well, I hope he's happy wherever he is. And we're all relieved now that we know what happened.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like everyone thinks Caribert left the village. That's probably for the best... At least they have some sort of explanation now.

choices.text: Caribert is gone. The Loom of Fate is now complete...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon wonders how Atossa's doing. Maybe we should go check on her? If she hasn't "remembered" like everyone else, we can tell her what happened.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't see her in the village just now, so... She's probably at the tree! C'mon, let's go talk to her!

choices.text: And no one else will try to change the villagers' memories.
Make sure you remember it this time.
Huh, I can't seem to remember...
He told me about the Loom of Fate.
I'm having trouble thinking straight right now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Atossa! How's it going?

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. I was just about to go looking for you. I wanted to thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: I was part of the search party, so I... remember what happened to Caribert now.

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Honestly... I just... can't believe I forgot something so important...

choices.text: Maybe he wanted you to forget him.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: He always seemed to appear out of nowhere, and now... he left just as quickly...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: If Caribert wants me to forget about the time we spent together, then I'm willing to try.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: I relied on him for a lot of things. But, I'm sure with enough time, even the deepest of attachments can fade.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "You must get along with each other, the two of you."

choices.text: I'm sure he wouldn't want you to forget him.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: It's funny, but... I have this feeling he told me the same thing. I just can't seem to remember when...

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: I guess it doesn't really matter, anyway. Life is made up of a series of memories. As long as I hold onto our time together... He'll always be a part of my life.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: I'm just happy I got to meet him. So, who cares what happens in the future, right?

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Okay, I'll admit, I'm just putting on a brave face.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: I was dumped... wasn't I?

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: ...Otherwise, why would he just leave like that without saying goodbye?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm sure... he had his reasons.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Hehe, you don't need to comfort me. I'll be okay.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: It's just like Caribert said... It's the things we overcome that make life more precious.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: And, y'know... If he has a heart, maybe he'll come back and see me one day.

response.speaker: Atossa
response.text: Anyway, thanks for all your hard work, you two. I promised I'd help Granny Jehiet with something, so I should head back. Goodbye!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... That should be it, right? Everyone's lives can go back to normal now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Weren't you about to tell Paimon what happened after your conversation with Caribert?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Right... What was it that happened...? I can't remember...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh? It feels like there's something in my pocket...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh. A picture? Where'd that come from? Let Paimon see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Paimon totally forgot about the Ley Line disturbances. We're in someone else's memory...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just like how you entered your sibling's memory last time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That would also explain why we seem to be at a time before he went missing... It's a memory, after all.

choices.text: If we really are in someone's memory...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! If he's someone who only exists in people's memories, then we're finally on the same turf!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, didn't Bahram just say he saw him leave the village with someone? Where should we go look for him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who knows how long this Ley Line disturbance is gonna last... We might not have that much time. And we don't even know whose memory this is...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go through what we know so far...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea! That'll help us narrow things down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We pretty much figured out that the missing villager has the ability to...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Implant memories into the minds of others.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, that! Could we try to figure out a bit more about him using what we know of his ability?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like, does it maybe leave a trace that would somehow give him away?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Hmm... Implanting memories into the minds of others must be an imperfect process. There's no way the new memories could perfectly blend in with the old ones. There has to be some kind of tell...)

choices.text: Then this is our chance to find him.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: A missing villager... Did I really forget something so important? As the chief, I can't afford to be so negligent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange... Bahram seems to remember him... And, apparently, he just saw him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think maybe... It's not that there's something wrong with people's memories, but that we've somehow returned to a time before he went missing?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I doubt returning to the past would be that simple.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Given everything Dain mentioned about disturbances with the Ley Lines, I'd say it's far more likely this is related to memories in some way...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I need to think carefully... What's really going on...?)

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: ...So, you see, Granny Jehiet was a mercenary when she was younger. She just talks like that out of habit. She's not trying to scare the children on purpose, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Oh, there I go again... always talking about my own things. Do you, maybe, have anything you want to share?

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Um... It's okay if you don't. You could also just... Talk about what you think of me?
Oh, I... I think you're an incredibly strong and thoughtful young woman.
You'll meet many amazing people and live a very happy life... You won't miss someone like me...

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Huh...? Are those your friends over there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We finally found him. But why does he look kind of familiar...?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right. This version of Atossa hasn't met us yet...
Friends? I guess you could say that. It must have taken them a lot of effort to find me...
So... I should see what they need. I'm sorry, Atossa. We'll have to continue this conversation another time.

dialogues.speaker: Atossa
dialogues.text: Another time, huh... Um, yeah! Okay! I'll head back to the village, then. Talk to you... some other time!
#It's nice to see you, {NICKNAME}. I believe this is the first time we've met.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Factoring in the memories, the Abyss Order, the Loom of Fate, and everything else, I need to think of the one person that can connect all of this together...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder! All this time, and the sky hasn't changed a bit. That must mean... Time isn't passing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the tell of the fake memories!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The implanted memories are basically taking place outside the regular twenty-four hours of the day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If the memories included the regular passage of time, it would be easy for people to tell that something was off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like, there could be overlap or something... People might start to wonder why they remember doing two different things at the same time of day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's why he makes sure the memories take place at a specific moment in time, rather than over a period of time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If we consider this in conjunction with what we already know, then the question of whose memory this is... seems to have an obvious answer...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Abyss Order's on the move... The Ley Lines are all out of whack...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We better hurry back to Vimara Village and see what's going on!
